idiom_name: class with #private fields and intent-named methods
implementation_notes: Since ES2022 a class can declare hard-private state with # fields and methods, enforced by the engine, so the classic structure is native: private state, a factory (JavaScript has no private constructor - use a static factory, optionally guarded by a private flag, or a module-scoped builder), getters that expose derived values, and command methods that keep invariants. Frozen plain objects serve value objects; the older closure/WeakMap emulation of privacy described in the class-fields proposal is no longer necessary, though factory functions remain a legitimate functional alternative.
pitfalls: Private fields are invisible to structuredClone, Object.freeze and object spread: copying or serialising an order silently loses its state - map through a dedicated mapper instead.
JSON round-trips drop the prototype, so revived objects are plain data; rebuild domain instances at the boundary rather than trusting the parsed shape.
Public class fields (no #) are writable by anything, including template engines and serializers that enumerate them.
